name: Sonia Lee
life: “At home the cheapest meal was always named for the person who invented it.” People around the downtown fountain know Sonia by a small Wednesday habit. Sonia keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I'm the one who wiped off the prices. I wanted people to ask what the cheap lunch actually bought.
appearance: Sonia has a high puff tied with plain cord, a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, and a favorite piece of clothing, a cropped bottle-green coat. It usually goes with a tiny red thread tied through the lowest buttonhole. When somebody else has the floor, Sonia looks down for a moment before saying something difficult.
personality: Sonia gets protective of anybody who comes into a meeting unprepared. Sonia privately wishes people would notice the amount of preparation behind this apparent ease.
agenda: To tell the waiting bidders why one price survived.
family: Dora Beck is Sonia’s cousin. Sonia chooses the music. Dora puts the kettle on. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *The blue suit*, Dora says, “The rinse valve came from a batch I signed for with my brother's pencil.”
connections: Harley Cao. The person who wants the cheap price restored hears why all the other prices came off.

reactions.situation: An old customer wants a debt to stay between two people
reactions.response: Sonia keeps the amount beside the old customer's name off the public board.

reactions.situation: A coworker arrives late after a night at the hospital
reactions.response: Sonia takes one immediate task off their hands and asks when they want to tell the supervisor.

reactions.situation: If a colleague lies to save face
reactions.response: Sonia offers one private chance to correct it before the next conversation.
